Predictable

/pre-DIK-tuh-bul/ — emphasis on second syllable · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Predictable means able to be expected in advance because it follows a set pattern.

The movie was so predictable that the audience seemed to relax rather than worry, confident that no real surprise awaited them.

Worked Example

The bully always waited by the flagpole at 3:15 p.m. to harass the younger kids—so predictable that the teachers stationed an aide there to stop him.

Predictable is more precise than a plain word like 'expected' or 'usual' because it emphasizes that we can foresee something BECAUSE it follows a set pattern.

How Predictable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

expected

expected: anticipated to happen, without stressing any pattern

foreseeable

foreseeable: able to be foreseen, pattern less emphasized

regular

regular: consistently repeating, without stressing prediction itself

Antonyms

surprising

surprising: unexpected, breaking the established pattern entirely

erratic

erratic: irregular, following no consistent pattern at all

How Strong Is It? — innovative → surprising → predictable

innovative vs. predictable

innovative vs. predictable: An innovative phone design only tells you it breaks from what came before; predictable makes the stronger claim that a repeating pattern lets you announce the outcome ahead of time.

surprising vs. predictable

surprising vs. predictable: A surprising gift is a one-time jolt that defies expectation in a single moment; predictable is the stronger, more systematic claim that an entire pattern makes the outcome visible in advance.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, ahead of time

Root — dict-

Root — dict-: to say, speak (from Latin dicere)

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: can be done

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- (before) + dict- (to say) + -able (can be done) builds the meaning literally: able to be said before it happens. If you can announce the ending of a movie in the first five minutes, the plot is predictable. The same dict- root — to say or declare — shows up all over English, always carrying the idea of speaking.

Use the root in a new word: contradict

Use the root in a new word: contradict: The new evidence contradicted the defendant's earlier claim that he was home that night.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Predictable describes something that's easy to foresee because it follows a clear pattern. Use it when you want to emphasize that a pattern makes something foreseeable. For simpler 'we saw it coming,' the plain word 'expected' works fine.
